title: 2009 HMMT February General Round 2 Problem 8
statement:
The incircle \(\omega\) of equilateral triangle \(A B C\) has radius 1. Three smaller circles are inscribed tangent to \(\omega\) and the sides of \(A B C\), as shown. Three smaller circles are then inscribed tangent to the previous circles and to each of two sides of \(A B C\). This process is repeated an infinite number of times. What is the total length of the circumferences of all the circles?

[Diagram omitted from this imported transcription; consult the HMMT archive while reviewing the problem.]

solutions.text: One can find using the Pythagorean Theorem that, in each iteration, the new circles have radius \(1 / 3\) of that of the previously drawn circles. Thus the total circumference is \(2 \pi+3 \cdot 2 \pi\left(\frac{1}{1-1 / 3}-1\right)=\) \(5 \pi\).
